en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.7. Indeterminate Resultants (Abyākatavipāka) 2.1.7.1.
The Five Sense-Consciousnesses that are Resultants of Wholesome Karma (Kusalavipākapañcaviññāṇa) Which phenomena are indeterminate (abyākata)?
At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated wholesome karma of the sense-sphere,
eye-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity with a visible form as its object— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind, and there is the mind-faculty.
There is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted, the quality of having contacted—
this, on that occasion, is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?

That which at that time is born of contact with the corresponding eye-consciousness element, mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant, born of mind-contact, a feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure, a feeling born of mind-contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this is the feeling at that time.
What kind of perception is there at that time? Whatever perception,
perceiving, state of having perceived, arises at that time born of contact with the corresponding eye-consciousness element—
that is the perception present at that time.
What on that occasion is volition?
That which on that occasion is volition, act-of-willing, state-of-having-willed born of contact with the corresponding visual consciousness-element—
this is the volition that there is on that occasion.
What on that occasion is consciousness (citta)?
That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness,
the element of visual-consciousness born thereof— this on that occasion is consciousness.
What is equanimity at that time?

That which at that time is mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant, born of mind-contact, a feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, a feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant—
this is equanimity at that time.
What on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind?
That which on that occasion is the stability of the mind—
this on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind (manindriya)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness (citta), mind (mano), mentation (mānasa), heart (hadaya), lucidity (paṇḍara), mind, the sphere of mind (manāyatana), the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of visual consciousness—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity?
That which on that occasion is mental neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, born of mental contact, a feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity.
What on that occasion is the life-faculty?
That which, for those immaterial states, is the life-span, the persistence, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the occurrence,
the preservation, the vitality, the life-faculty— this on that occasion is the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are three faculties, there is one contact ... [and so on] ...
there is one eye-consciousness element, there is one base of mental phenomena, there is one element of mental phenomena;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate …pe….
What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the feeling aggregate, excluding the perception aggregate, and excluding the consciousness aggregate—
this, at that time, is the formations aggregate.
…pe… These phenomena are indeterminate.
Which states are indeterminate?

At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere, there arises resultant ear-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with sound as its object;
… pe … there arises resultant nose-consciousness accompanied by equanimity with odor as its object; … pe …
Tongue-consciousness arises accompanied by equanimity, having taste as its object...
tactile consciousness arises accompanied by pleasure, having a tangible object as its object.
At that time, there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is mind, there is pleasure, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the mind faculty, there is the pleasure faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the state of being contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?

Whatever bodily pleasure, bodily happiness, pleasant and happy experience born of contact with the body, and pleasant and happy feeling born of contact with the body, arising from that specific body-consciousness-element at that time—
that is the feeling at that time.
What kind of perception is present at that time?
Whatever perception, perceiving, state of having perceived, arises at that time born of contact with the corresponding body-consciousness element—
this is the perception present at that time.
What is volition at that time?
That which at that time is volition born of contact with the corresponding body-consciousness element, volitional act, the state of having willed—
this is the volition at that time.
What on that occasion is consciousness (citta)?
That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness,
the element of body-consciousness produced by that— this on that occasion is consciousness.
What is the pleasure at that time?
Whatever bodily ease, bodily pleasure, pleasant feeling born of body-contact, and pleasant, comfortable sensation born of body-contact there is at that time—
this is the pleasure at that time.
What at that time is one-pointedness of mind?
That which at that time is the stability of the mind—
this at that time is one-pointedness of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind (manindriya)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness (citta), mind (mano), mentation (mānasa), heart (hadaya), lucidity (paṇḍara), mind, the mind-base (manāyatana), the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of body-consciousness—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of pleasure?
That which on that occasion is bodily well-being, bodily pleasure, the pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of body-contact, the pleasant and pleasurable sensation born of body-contact—
this on that occasion is the faculty of pleasure.
What on that occasion is the life-faculty (*jīvitindriya*)?
That which, for those immaterial states, is the life-span, the duration, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the persistence, the preservation, the vitality, the life-faculty—
this on that occasion is the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are three faculties, there is one contact … [and so on] … there is one body-consciousness element,
there is one mental-object base, there is one mental-object element;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the feeling aggregate, excluding the perception aggregate, and excluding the consciousness aggregate—
this, at that time, is the formations aggregate.
…pe… These phenomena are indeterminate.
The five types of wholesome-resultant consciousness.
2.1.7.2. Wholesome-resultant mind-element.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere, the resultant mind-element arises accompanied by equanimity,

having either a visible form as its object, or … [as above] … tangible objects as its object, or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the mind faculty, there is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the state of being contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?
That which at that time is born of contact with the mind-element, mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant, born of mind-contact, a feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure born of mind-contact—
this is the feeling at that time.
What kind of perception is there at that time?
Whatever perception, perceiving, state of having perceived, arises at that time born of contact with the corresponding mind-element—
that is the perception present at that time.
What is volition at that time?
That which at that time is volition born of mind-element-contact, volitional formation, the state of having willed—
this is the volition at that time.
What on that occasion is consciousness (citta)?
That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness,
the element of mind-consciousness born thereof— this on that occasion is consciousness.
What is applied thought at that time?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, sustained application, and the directing of the mind—
this is the applied thought at that time.
What at that time is sustained thought (vicāra)?
That which at that time is moving about, sustained thought, close examination, mental scrutiny, the state of following after the mind, the state of looking around—
it is this that at that time is sustained thought.
What on that occasion is equanimity (upekkhā)?
That which on that occasion is mental neither-pleasure-nor-displeasure, born of mental contact, a feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this on that occasion is equanimity.
What on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind?
That which on that occasion is the stability of the mind—
this on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind?
That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, the mind base, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness,
the mind element born thereof— this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity?

That which on that occasion is mental neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, neither agreeable nor disagreeable, born of mental contact, the feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity.
What on that occasion is the life-faculty?
That which, for those immaterial states, is the life-span, the persistence, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the occurrence,
the preservation, the vitality, the life-faculty— this on that occasion is the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are three faculties, there is one contact …pe… there is one mind-element,
there is one mental-object base, there is one mental-object element;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty.

Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena there are at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—
this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations.
…pe… These phenomena are indeterminate.
The wholesome resultant mind-element.
2.1.7.3. Wholesome resultant mind-consciousness-element accompanied by joy.
Which phenomena are indeterminate (abyākata)?

At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere, the resultant mind-consciousness element arises accompanied by joy, having either a visible form as its object …pe… or a mental phenomenon as its object,
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness,
there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is rapture, and there is pleasure.
There is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of mental pleasure, there is the life-faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the quality of having contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?

Whatever mental pleasantness, mental happiness, pleasant and happy experience born of contact with the mind-consciousness element produced by those [conditions], the pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact—
that is the feeling at that time.
What is perception at that time? Whatever perception,
perceiving, state of having perceived, arises at that time born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element—
this is perception at that time.
What is volition at that time?
That which at that time is volition born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element, the state of being volitional,
the state of having willed— this is the volition at that time.
What is the state of mind at that time?

That which at that time is mind, intellect, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this is the state of mind at that time.
What is applied thought at that time?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, focused application, the directing of the mind—
this is the applied thought at that time.
What at that time is sustained thought (vicāra)?
That which at that time is movement, sustained thought, following after, close following, the continuous threading of the mind, the close examination—
it is this that at that time is sustained thought.
What on that occasion is rapture (pīti)?
That which on that occasion is rapture, gladness, rejoicing, rejoicing of mind, joy, mirth, felicity, elation, mental upliftment—
this on that occasion is rapture.
What is the pleasure at that time?
Whatever at that time is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mind-contact, a pleasant and pleasurable sensation born of mind-contact—
this is the pleasure at that time.
What on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind?
That which on that occasion is the stability of the mind—
this on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind (manindriya)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness (citta), mind (mano), mentation (mānasa), heart (hadaya), lucidity (paṇḍara), mind, the sphere of mind (manāyatana), the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness,
and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness— this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mental joy (somanassindriya)?
That which on that occasion is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and joyful feeling born of mind-contact, a pleasant and joyful sensation born of mind-contact—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mental joy.
What on that occasion is the life-faculty (*jīvitindriya*)?
That which, for those immaterial states, is the life-span, the duration, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the persistence, the preservation, the vitality, the life-faculty—
this on that occasion is the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are three faculties, there is one contact … [as before] … there is one mind-consciousness element,
there is one base of mental phenomena, there is one element of mental phenomena;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty.

Or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*). ...pe...
These phenomena are indeterminate (*abyākata*).
The wholesome-resultant mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy.
2.1.7.4. Wholesome-resultant mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity.
Which phenomena are indeterminate (abyākata)?

At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere, the resultant mind-consciousness element arises accompanied by equanimity, having either a visible form as its object … or mental phenomena as its object,
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the mind faculty, there is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the quality of having contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?

That which at that time is born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element, a mental state that is neither pleasant nor unpleasant, a feeling born of mental contact that is neither painful nor pleasant—a feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant:
this is the feeling at that time.
What is perception at that time? Whatever perception,
perceiving, state of having perceived, arises at that time born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element—
this is perception at that time.
What at that time is volition?
That which at that time is volition born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element, the act of intending, the state of having intended—
this at that time is volition.
What on that occasion is consciousness (citta)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind (mano), mentation (mānasa), heart (hadaya), lucidity (paṇḍara), mind, mind-base (manāyatana), mind-faculty (manindriya), consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness,
the element of mind-consciousness born thereof— this on that occasion is consciousness.
What is applied thought (vitakka) at that time?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, focused application, the directing of the mind—
this is the applied thought at that time.
What at that time is sustained thought (*vicāra*)?
That which at that time is movement, sustained thought, following after, close following, the mental state of continuous connection, and the state of close observation—
this at that time is sustained thought.
What on that occasion is equanimity (upekkhā)?

That which on that occasion is mental neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, neither agreeable nor disagreeable, born of mental contact, the feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this on that occasion is equanimity.
What on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind?
That which on that occasion is the stability of the mind—
this on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind (manindriya)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, the sphere of mind, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the element of mind-consciousness born thereof—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity?

That which on that occasion is mental neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, neither agreeable nor disagreeable, born of mental contact, the feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity.
What at that time is the life-faculty?
That which, for those immaterial phenomena, is the life-span, the persistence, the maintenance, the upkeep, the carrying on, the subsistence, the preservation, the life, and the life-faculty—
this at that time is the life-faculty.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are indeterminate.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are three faculties, there is one contact …pe… there is one mind-consciousness element,
there is one base of mental phenomena, there is one element of mental phenomena;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time.
These states are indeterminate … [as above] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, and the life-faculty.

Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations. ...
These phenomena are indeterminate.
The wholesome-resultant mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity.
2.1.7.5. The Eight Great Resultants.
Which phenomena are indeterminate (abyākata)?

At whatever time, as a result of having performed and accumulated wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere, the resultant mind-consciousness element arises accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge … [or] accompanied by joy,
associated with knowledge, and with volitional effort … [or] accompanied by joy and dissociated from knowledge … [and so forth].
Accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with mental effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge, with mental effort … [and so on].
Accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge …pe… accompanied by equanimity,
dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort, having visible form as its object …pe… or having mental phenomena as its object,
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe…
These states are indeterminate …pe… non-greed is an indeterminate root …pe… non-hatred is an indeterminate root …pe…
These phenomena are indeterminate (abyākata).
The eight great resultant [consciousnesses]. 2.1.7.6. Rūpāvacara-resultant [consciousness].
Which states are indeterminate?

At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures … [as before] … and, having attained the first jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa, dwells therein— at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before] … these states are wholesome.
As a result of having performed and accumulated that very wholesome kamma pertaining to the fine-material sphere, he—secluded from sensual pleasures...
[as before] ...enters and dwells in the first jhāna with the earth-kasiṇa; at that time there is contact...
[as before] ...there is non-distraction... [as before].
These phenomena are indeterminate.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?

At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought … [as before] … one enters and dwells in the second jhāna … [as before] … these phenomena are indeterminate.
the third jhāna … the fourth jhāna … the first jhāna … and so forth.
He enters and dwells in the fifth jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa; at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … these states are wholesome.
Due to the performance and accumulation of that very same wholesome karma of the fine-material sphere, as its result, with the abandoning of pleasure … [and so on] …
... pe ... he enters and dwells in the fifth jhāna with the earth-kasiṇa; at that time there is contact ...
pe ... there is non-distraction ... pe ...
these states are indeterminate.
The results of the fine-material sphere. 2.1.7.7.
The results of the immaterial sphere.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm— by completely transcending perceptions of form,
by the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, by non-attention to perceptions of diversity, and with the perception of the base of infinite space,
having abandoned pleasure … [and so on] … and attaining and dwelling in the fourth jhāna— at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on].
These states are wholesome.

As the result of that same wholesome karma of the formless sphere having been performed and accumulated, there arises the ripening consciousness accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite space,
through the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, and non-attention to perceptions of diversity.
With the abandoning of pleasure … [and so on] … he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna;
at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … these states are indeterminate.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of infinite space,
accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite consciousness, and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … having entered and dwelt in the fourth jhāna—
At that time there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction … pe … these states are wholesome.
Through the performance and accumulation of that very wholesome kamma of the formless sphere, its result is entirely the base of infinite space.
Having completely transcended the perception accompanied by the base of infinite consciousness, with the abandoning of pleasure ... [as before] ...
he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna; at that time there is contact ... [as before] ... there is non-distraction ...
[as before] ... these states are indeterminate.
Which phenomena are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness,
accompanied by the perception of the base of nothingness, and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … entering and dwelling in the fourth jhāna—
...dwells; at that time there is contact ...pe... there is non-distraction ...pe...
these states are wholesome.
Through the performance and accumulation of that very same wholesome karma of the formless sphere, its result is the base of infinite consciousness in every respect.
Having completely transcended the perception associated with the base of nothingness, with the abandoning of pleasure ... [and so on] ...
he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna; at that time there is contact ... [and so on] ... there is non-distraction ...
these states are indeterminate.
Which states are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of nothingness,
accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … entering and dwelling in the fourth jhāna.
At that time, there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are wholesome.
Through the performance and accumulation of that very same wholesome karma pertaining to the formless realm, its result is the sphere of nothingness in its entirety.
Having completely surmounted the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, with the abandoning of pleasure ... [as before] ...
he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna; at that time there is contact ... [as before] ... there is non-distraction ...
[as before] ... these states are indeterminate.
The resultant [consciousness] of the formless realm.
